name: @eiler2005/slidecraft

tools.name: list_exhibits
tools.description: Route the intended relationship (comparison, process, architecture, bridge) to existing layout contracts. Storyline and theme are independent choices.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: Existing native body exhibits with schemas and examples. Assemble complementary exhibits using layout: composition; keep title, sources and page numbering in the shared frame.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: How to make a deck with SlideCraft: the steps, the four checkpoints and the rules. Call this first.

tools.name: list_decks
tools.description: Decks in the workspace

tools.name: new_deck
tools.description: Start a deck from a goal in plain words; creates brief.yaml and deck.yaml in the workspace

goal.description: What the deck must achieve, e.g. "The board approves entry into Germany"

tools.name: suggest_templates
tools.description: Three template options (storyline × theme) and recommended outputs for the deck brief

tools.name: choose_template
tools.description: Record the chosen option (A, B or C) or an explicit storyline and theme

tools.name: scaffold
tools.description: Create the ghost deck (one slide per storyline slot) from the chosen template

tools.name: read_deck
tools.description: The deck.yaml text

tools.name: write_deck
tools.description: Replace deck.yaml with new YAML, then validate it and return the diagnostics

tools.name: list_layouts
tools.description: Slide layouts and their content contracts (JSON Schema with limits and an example). Pass a layout id for one.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Lay out the deck and run every check (fit, titles, sources, consistency, contrast); no files written

tools.name: fix_tasks
tools.description: Fields that are too long, each with an exact character budget

tools.name: apply_fixes
tools.description: Write rewrites by JSON pointer (comments kept) and re-check

tools.name: preview_slide
tools.description: Inspect a slide: resvg previews the Scene; pptx-convert renders the actual PPTX through installed Office. Scene previews do not certify PowerPoint fidelity.

renderer.description: Default resvg; pptx-convert requires Office and Poppler

tools.name: build
tools.description: Build the deck files (pptx, pdf, html, onepager, docx, png); returns the paths

tools.name: ingest
tools.description: Add client documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV) as sources with page-level references

tools.name: find
tools.description: Find a phrase in the ingested documents; each hit carries the citation to use, e.g. annual-report#p14

tools.name: import_pptx
tools.description: Turn an existing PowerPoint into a draft deck in the workspace (to restyle it)

tools.name: sync_pptx
tools.description: Bring text someone edited in the built PPTX back into deck.yaml. Without apply it only lists the changes — show them to the user, then call again with apply: true

instructions:
SlideCraft makes consulting-grade decks: answer first, action titles, the right exhibit, sources on every number, a partner-style review.

Work in this order and stop at each ✅ to ask the user:
1. ✅ Brief — new_deck(goal, audience). Ask what the deck must achieve, for whom, and what they will do with it (send as PDF, edit together, present).
2. ✅ Template — suggest_templates(deck), show the three options, then choose_template(deck, option).
3. ✅ Titles — scaffold(deck), then read_deck/write_deck: write one action title per slide (a full-sentence claim). Show the numbered title chain; revise until approved.
4. Build — for each slide fill the content using list_layouts(layout) contracts; write_deck; check(deck). Put client numbers in `facts:` and use {{id}} in text; read spreadsheets with `from: { file, sheet, range }`; cite sources as `id#p14` (ingest + find).
5. ✅ Review — check(deck) until no errors (use fix_tasks/apply_fixes for long text), preview_slide for each slide, then build(deck) and give the user the file paths.
If the user edited the PPTX by hand, sync_pptx brings the text back before the next build.
Never invent numbers or sources; flag gaps instead.
